title: Integrated balanced homodyne detector using CMOS capacitive-feedback TIA for quantum measurements
authors: Sarah Bastiaens, Cedric Bruynsteen, Simone Cammarata, Axl Bomhals, Leandro da Silva, Michiel Van Osta, Johan Bauwelinck, Xin Yin
abstract: A low-noise, high-speed balanced homodyne detector is demonstrated, combining a capacitive-feedback transimpedance amplifier implemented in 28 nm CMOS with a custom photonic integrated circuit fabricated in imec's iSiPP200 silicon photonics platform. The receiver achieves a 3-dB bandwidth of 7.6 GHz, a maximum shot noise clearance of 27 dB, a shot noise-limited bandwidth of 13.7 GHz and a common-mode rejection ratio up to 54.8 dB. These results demonstrate the suitability of CMOS capacitive-feedback transimpedance amplifiers for demanding quantum and coherent sensing optical applications, including continuous-variable quantum key distribution, quantum random number generation, and optical coherence tomography.
summary: This paper reports the successful demonstration of a high-speed, low-noise balanced homodyne detector by co-integrating a CMOS capacitive-feedback TIA with a silicon photonic chip. The resulting system achieves excellent performance metrics, including a 7.6 GHz bandwidth and 27 dB shot noise clearance. This integration proves the viability of CMOS technology for demanding quantum optical sensing applications.
main_problem: The core challenge is detecting and processing extremely weak optical signals, necessary for quantum measurements, while maintaining performance near the quantum-noise limit.
main_result: The authors demonstrated a high-performance, low-noise balanced homodyne detector achieving a 7.6 GHz 3-dB bandwidth and a maximum shot noise clearance of 27 dB.
method: The system integrates a capacitive-feedback transimpedance amplifier (TIA) fabricated in 28 nm CMOS directly with a silicon photonic integrated circuit (PIC).
model_or_system: The physical system is a Balanced Homodyne Detector (BHD) utilizing a PIC on the iSiPP200 platform and a CMOS TIA. The TIA employs a capacitive-feedback topology to minimize resistor thermal noise.
key_observables: 3-dB bandwidth (7.6 GHz), maximum shot noise clearance (27 dB), shot noise-limited bandwidth (13.7 GHz), and Common-Mode Rejection Ratio (up to 54.8 dB).
important_parameters: 28 nm CMOS technology, iSiPP200 silicon photonics platform, and the capacitive-feedback TIA topology.
main_assumptions: Analytical noise models assume simplifications like C2 >> C1 and A0 >> 1; the system also faces limitations from PD quantum efficiency and fabrication tolerances.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the BHD schematic, the TIA topology, noise analysis comparing analytical and simulated noise, and measured performance metrics like output noise PSD and CMRR vs. frequency.
paper_structure: The paper details the co-design approach, analyzes the TIA noise sources and compares feedback topologies, presents the BHD characterization via S-parameter and noise measurements, and concludes with a summary of the achieved high-performance metrics.
why_interesting: This work provides a highly integrated, low-power platform for quantum optics measurements, directly addressing the hardware requirements for continuous-variable quantum key distribution and quantum sensing.
